name: Hirkan National Park
blurb: Ancient Hyrcanian beech forest, wild boar, and the leopard that still roams it.

tip.title: Remove the leopard
tip.text: Take out the Caucasian leopard and see boar, roe deer and porcupine lose a predator, and the jackal lose a source of carrion.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light for the forest canopy; the humid subtropical lowlands and cooler mountain slopes share the same energy source.
Annual rainfall of roughly 1,400 to 1,800 mm, the highest in Azerbaijan, keeps the forest lush.
Leaf litter and dead wood return nutrients to the soil, feeding the trees again.
Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down leaf litter, dead wood and carcasses.
The dominant tree at mid elevations of the Hyrcanian forest. Its nuts feed boar and other animals.

nodes.name: European hornbeam
nodes.desc: A broadleaf tree of the Hyrcanian forest; GloBI records several birds eating it.
An omnivore that eats acorns and beechnuts, roots and carrion, and is hunted by wolves and leopards.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: A small deer of the forest that browses leaves and buds. Wolves and leopards take it.
An opportunist that eats small animals and fruit and scavenges the kills of wolves and leopards.
A small predator of birds and other animals, found in the park.
A large omnivore of the Hyrcanian forest. It eats nuts, fruit and other foods.

nodes.name: Caucasian leopard
nodes.desc: Camera traps have photographed it in Hirkan. Elsewhere in its range it preys on boar, roe deer and porcupine.
A top predator of the Hyrcanian forest, and the main predator of wild boar across much of its range.

story: Hirkan National Park covers 40,358 hectares in the Talysh region of Azerbaijan. Established in 2004 and enlarged in 2008, the park is 99% covered by forests in a mountainous region and protects humid subtropical and temperate forests.
matters: The park belongs to the Caspian Hyrcanian mixed forests ecoregion and shelters many endemic plant and animal species, including the Caucasian leopard.
